title: The Business Plan
summary: Why a business plan is needed, its main sections, SWOT analysis, calculating costs, income and profit for a small business, and sources of finance.

notes.text: A written document that describes a business idea, its goals, how it will be run and marketed, and its expected costs, income and profit.

items: It helps the entrepreneur think carefully about whether the idea will work.
It is needed to obtain **finance** from banks or investors.
It sets goals and is used to measure progress.
It identifies problems and risks before they happen.

rows: A short overview of the whole plan
Name, location, form of ownership, the product or service, vision and mission
Target market, customer needs, competitors, SWOT analysis
The 4 Ps: product, price, place and promotion
How the product is made or the service delivered; equipment and suppliers
Who runs the business, staff needed and their duties
Start-up costs, expected income and expenses, break-even point, source of capital
**Strengths**: what the business does well (e.g. skilled owner, good location)
**Opportunities**: chances in the environment to use (e.g. no competitors nearby, new school opening)
**Weaknesses**: what the business lacks (e.g. little capital, no experience)
**Threats**: dangers outside the business (e.g. load-shedding, new competitor, rising prices)

items: **Fixed costs** stay the same no matter how much is produced: rent, insurance, salaries.
**Variable costs** change with the amount produced: ingredients, packaging, electricity used for production.

notes.latex: \text{break-even quantity} = \frac{\text{fixed costs}}{\text{selling price per unit} - \text{variable cost per unit}}

notes.title: A vetkoek business
notes.problem: Zodwa sells vetkoek for R8 each. Ingredients cost R3 per vetkoek. Her fixed costs (stall rent and gas bottle) are R1 500 per month. (a) How many must she sell to break even? (b) What is her profit if she sells 600 in a month?

notes.title: Working out a month's profit
notes.problem: A muffin seller sells 200 muffins at R12 each. Ingredients cost R5 per muffin and the stall costs R500 a month. Calculate the profit.
steps: Costs that depend on sales: 200 × R5 = R1 000.
notes.answer: A profit of R900 for the month.

items: **Government agencies** such as the **National Youth Development Agency (NYDA)** and the Small Enterprise Development and Finance Agency (SEDFA), which help young and small entrepreneurs.
